summary: Frontend-only mobile-first verification executed on preview URL. Stable planned minutes and curriculum alignment passed; unavailable-day restore flow failed in web preview.

integration_issues.flow: Schedule future day -> Mark unavailable -> then Mark available
integration_issues.issue: After tapping Mark unavailable, day did not switch to UNAVAILABLE state and Mark available control never appeared, so restore path could not execute.

action_items: Fix Schedule unavailable flow in web preview so Mark unavailable actually applies date override and surfaces Mark available state.
Re-test unavailable->available lifecycle after fix with the same future-day scenario.
Consider replacing Alert-based critical confirmations with a cross-platform in-app confirm modal for Expo web parity.
critical_code_review_comments: In /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/schedule.tsx, critical state transitions are behind Alert.alert callbacks; observed web behavior indicates callback path is not executing in preview for Mark unavailable.
In /app/frontend/app/_layout.tsx, LogBox.ignoreAllLogs(true) suppresses warnings/errors and can hide regressions during QA.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Tested on https://emergent-code-sync.preview.emergentagent.com at 375x667 with fresh local storage + onboarding (weekday/sat/sun=240). Today planned remained 225m before/after completing first task. First two tasks matched expected sequence and IDs: task-card-s1-d1-t1, task-card-s1-d1-t2. Curriculum static validation confirmed 250 tasks and correct Sprint/Original Day metadata mapping.
rca_of_issue: Repro: open Schedule tab, select a future day (today+2), tap Mark unavailable. Expected day to become unavailable and show Mark available. Actual: no unavailable state/control change. Likely root cause is the web execution path of Alert-based confirmation not invoking the destructive callback in this environment, preventing markUnavailable() from running. Mitigation: use a custom in-app confirmation modal and call markUnavailable/markAvailable directly from modal actions for web/native consistency.
